paths.description: Localized homepage and primary news-discovery surface; represents the global shell, navigation, cards, consent and advertising.
Current long-form/list article; represents editorial reading, article metadata and server rendering.
Live scores surface; represents the primary interactive sports-data journey and repeated scrolling.
Arsenal team overview; represents entity/detail pages with standings and news.
Deliberately invalid route; represents HTTP/navigation failure recovery.

findings.summary: A full-page consent/pay wall obscures the primary article before any interaction.
findings.evidence: Desktop article screenshot shows an 870×676 consent surface over dimmed editorial content; the mobile scores screenshot is entirely occupied by the same choice.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep core content visible and offer a compact, dismissible consent choice with equally prominent accept and reject controls; use a semantic dialog only when true modality is required.

findings.summary: The consent flow presents “Accept All & Continue” as the only free path; rejection is coupled to a £3.49 monthly payment.
findings.evidence: Load screenshots show two primary choices: accept personalized advertising for free or “Reject & Pay”; no free reject-all control is visible despite 252 technology partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a free, equally prominent reject-all option and move the optional ad-free subscription into a separate, clearly described purchase flow.

findings.summary: The site forces its stored dark theme instead of following the system light/dark preference on first visit.
findings.evidence: Dark and light emulation screenshots are byte-identical (660,976 bytes each); the DOM probe reports theme="dark" and computed colorScheme="normal".
findings.suggestedFix: Default to prefers-color-scheme, declare color-scheme: light dark, and only override it after an explicit user theme choice.

findings.summary: Indefinite pulse animations continue when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, getAnimations() still reported running pulse1 and pulse2 animations with 3,000 ms duration and unbounded iterations.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable non-essential pulsing and auto-motion inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce), retaining only instant state changes.

findings.summary: The homepage misses the good LCP range by a wide margin.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP at 14.0 s (performance 47); the independent trace measured LCP at 4.87 s and FCP at 2.45 s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP image/content, reduce document latency and competing work, and verify LCP below 2.5 s on mobile.

findings.summary: Startup JavaScript blocks the main thread.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported 410 ms TBT; the trace found three long tasks, 206 ms TBT and a longest task of 208.87 ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the long tasks, split work below 50 ms, defer non-critical hydration/ads, and schedule low-priority work after the main content.

findings.summary: The initial load has a large fragmented critical path.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 145 requests and 2.62 MB transferred, including 62 scripts (1.10 MB), 52 images (1.15 MB), and at least nine parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheets confirmed by DOM CSS links.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate and inline only critical CSS, defer non-critical styles/scripts, reduce initial route chunks, and gate consent/ad code until needed.

findings.summary: Image delivery is frequently oversized or lacks intrinsic dimensions.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 63 of 100 images without width/height, 28 oversized images, 99 legacy-format URLs, and 2 images without responsive sources.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic dimensions and responsive srcset/sizes, request display-appropriate CDN widths, and negotiate AVIF/WebP while preserving fallbacks.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS, but HSTS is absent and CSP allows unsafe script execution.
findings.evidence: Headers primitive found no Strict-Transport-Security header; CSP script-src allows both unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy HSTS after subdomain readiness and migrate scripts to nonces/hashes so unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval can be removed.

findings.summary: The default experience exposes a large partner/third-party surface before a humane consent choice.
findings.evidence: Consent copy names 252 technology partners; network evidence found six third-party origins, while the only observed cookie used SameSite=None for 365 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize partners and pre-consent calls, document necessity per vendor, shorten cookie lifetime, and only load optional analytics/ads after freely given consent.

findings.summary: The homepage emits numerous browser console errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse errors-in-console audit failed with 28 recorded items.
findings.suggestedFix: Triage and remove the production console errors, beginning with failed requests and uncaught application/third-party exceptions.

findings.summary: Icon-only controls and links lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed button-name (4 elements) and link-name (2 elements); the scores probe found multiple 16–35 px buttons with empty text and null/empty aria-label.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every icon control a stable accessible name using visible text or aria-label, and ensure linked card images inherit the story title.

findings.summary: The homepage has no H1 and begins its content hierarchy at H2/H3.
findings.evidence: DOM quality probe found zero H1 elements on the homepage, while article, team, and scores templates each expose one descriptive H1.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a single descriptive homepage H1, visually integrated with the lead section, and preserve a logical nested heading order.

findings.summary: Many interactive targets are below comfortable touch size.
findings.evidence: The home probe counted 51 visible controls below 24 px in one dimension; the live-scores probe measured date/action buttons around 35.7×32 px and several icon buttons at 16×16 px.
findings.suggestedFix: Expand interactive hit areas to at least 44×44 CSS px where space permits, without enlarging icons, and retain visible :focus-visible styling.

findings.summary: The viewport policy limits user zoom and combines with undersized targets.
findings.evidence: The homepage viewport is width=device-width, initial-scale=1, maximum-scale=1; target probes found 51 sub-24 px controls despite mobile layout itself having no overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale=1 and verify 200–400% zoom/reflow while increasing target hit areas.

findings.summary: The modal consent surface is not represented by native dialog/popover semantics in the inspected document.
findings.evidence: A blocking modal is visible in screenshots, but the rendered DOM probe found zero dialog elements, zero popovers and zero details elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a native dialog with correctly managed focus for true modality, or a non-modal disclosure when consent need not block reading.

findings.summary: The site advertises a web manifest but no active service worker or usable manifest payload was observed.
findings.evidence: DOM links site.webmanifest, but the platform probe found zero service-worker registrations and could not parse a manifest payload.
findings.suggestedFix: If app-like installation is intentional, serve a valid manifest and register a small service worker with an offline reading/error fallback; otherwise remove misleading install signals.

findings.summary: Third-party and consent code consumes a material portion of an already heavy initial load.
findings.evidence: HAR measured 2.62 MB across 145 requests; consent JS alone was about 95 KB, with six third-party origins and 12 consent-host requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Set per-route third-party budgets, defer optional vendors until consent and interaction, and remove partners that do not provide measurable user value.

findings.summary: Editorial and live-score capabilities are machine-readable as HTML but are not exposed as structured agent tools.
findings.evidence: Discoverability is strong (77% homepage, 95% article) and metadata is rich, but DOM/platform probes expose no WebMCP or agent-tool registration.
findings.suggestedFix: Treat this as an emerging opportunity: expose read-only score lookup/search tools with explicit schemas and safe authorization boundaries.

taskList.title: Replace pay-or-track blocking consent with a free, symmetric and dismissible choice
Bring LCP below 2.5 s by shrinking and reprioritising the initial route
Restore accessible names, target sizes, heading hierarchy and zoom
Harden transport policy with HSTS and nonce/hash-based CSP
Optimize responsive images and set a third-party transfer budget
Follow system theme and remove non-essential motion under reduced-motion
Clarify PWA intent and add offline fallback or remove install signals
Explore safe read-only WebMCP tools for scores and search
